chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I sought permission for one of our companions to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he asked him about al-nabidh, so he said: 'It is permissible.' He said: 'May Allah keep you well, I only asked you about the nabidh in which the residue is placed and it boils until it intoxicates.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every intoxicant is forbidden.'
The man said: 'May Allah keep you well, for those with us in Iraq say that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) only meant by that the cup that intoxicates.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, a little of it is forbidden.'
The man said to him: 'What if we dilute it with water?'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and it is not for the water to make permissible that which is forbidden. Fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not drink it.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh (fermented drink of water and fruit/dates)
key_terms.كَثِيرُهُ فَقَلِيلُهُ: A lot of it and a little of it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on nabidh if it intoxicates?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of al-nabidh by establishing the principle of 'kathiruhu wa qaliluhu haram' (its abundant and scanty amounts are both forbidden) once intoxication occurs, refuting the Iraqi school's view that only the concentrated cup is prohibited. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) further emphasizes that dilution with water does not render the intoxicant permissible, underscoring the intrinsic nature of the prohibition. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the threshold of intoxication in fermented beverages.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I sought permission for one of our companions to Abu Abdullahasws, so he asked himasws about Al Nabeez, so heasws said: ‘Permissible’. So he said, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! But rather I ask youasws about Al-Nabeez in which the residue is made to be, so it boils until it intoxicates’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is prohibited’.

So the man said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! So there are ones with us at Al-Iraq who are saying that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, rather meant by that the cup which intoxicates’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever a lot of it were to intoxicate, so a little of it is Prohibited’.
So the man said to himasws, ‘Supposing most of it is the water?’
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, and it is not for the water that is should make Permissible (that which is) Prohibited. Fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and do not drink it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘ Abd af-Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj who has said the following: “

I once asked for permission from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, for a certain person of our people and he asked him (the Imam) about al-Nabidh. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is lawful.’ He said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, I asked about al-Nabidh which is placed in al-‘Akr (murky) to boil until it becomes intoxicating.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘All intoxicating liquor is unlawful.’
He said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, among us in Iraq they say that the Messenger of Allah thereby meant the cup that is intoxicating liquor.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Whatever is intoxicating liquor in large quantity, it is unlawful in small quantity also.’
He (the man) then said, ‘Can I break it (intoxicating effect) with water?’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘No, how can water make lawful what is unlawful? Have fear of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and do not drink it.’”
